rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a TiC-reinforced composite coating, while the paper used a WNbMoTaV refractory high-entropy alloy coating. This is a different kind of intervention (composition change vs. RHEA coating).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies room-temperature dry sliding wear via ball-on-disk tests, whereas the paper used linear reciprocating wear with a Si3N4 ball under 20 N. Both are room-temperature sliding wear, but the specific test configuration and load differ.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes hard particle reinforcement, dislocation impedance, and load-bearing by TiC, while the paper's mechanism relies on lattice distortion, solid-solution strengthening, grain refinement, and tribo-oxide formation in a BCC solid solution. These are different general classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased hardness (25-40%) and reduced wear rate (~50%), while the paper found hardness increases of 72-97% and wear resistance improvements of 83-242%. Both predict the right property and direction, but the magnitude is substantially different.
